chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madaini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Do not keep a hunting dog in the house except if there is a door between you and it.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for keeping a hunting dog inside the house according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines a specific condition for keeping hunting dogs indoors, requiring a physical barrier (a door) to separate the animal from the living space. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling is often linked to maintaining ritual purity (taharah) by preventing the dog's saliva or fur from contaminating the main area of the house, reflecting the practical concerns of domestic life in early Islamic society.
